description: A light to medium-weight hardwood, pale yellowish-brown, with some logs showing dark grey-brown streaks sold as black limba. Used for furniture, frames, drawer sides, veneer, plywood, and electric guitar bodies.

hazards.summary: HSE lists reduced lung function and bleeding from the nose and gums among reported effects of limba dust.
HSE lists nettle rash (itchy, raised welts) from contact with limba.
HSE notes that limba splinter wounds can turn septic.
A review of wood allergy lists limba as a reported cause of occupational asthma, based on German case reports that could not be checked for this page.
IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, chiefly through cancers of the nose and sinuses. This applies to limba dust as it does to any other wood.

image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed limba (Terminalia superba) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Pale straw to light yellowish-brown wood with a few irregular dark grey-brown to black streaks running along the board. Mostly straight grain, moderately coarse texture with open pores, and a medium natural luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of limba with pale yellowish-brown wood crossed by a few irregular dark streaks.
notes_internal: Asthma primaries listed by Schlunssen-2018 (Oertmann 1993 Allergologie 16:334-340; Kersten 1994 Allergologie 17:55-60; Wirtz 1997 Arbeitsmed Sozialmed Umweltmed 32:257-260, 'Asthmaanfalle durch Abachi- und Limbaholz') are not in PubMed or Crossref and were not read, so Tier B is cited at level 3. Upgrade if a library copy of Wirtz-1997 confirms challenge testing.
